entries.body: Psalm 27:1 says, “By David. The LORD is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? The LORD is the strength of my life. entries.body: Romans 8:28 says, “We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose.” Isolation gives harmful patterns more room to grow. Recovery deepens through honest connection—with God, with wise helpers, and with people who can remind you of hope when your own voice is tired. Let this verse shape the next decision rather than asking it to fix the entire journey at once.
entries.prayer: Present God, help me receive your care and recognize the people you have placed beside me.
entries.practice: Identify one person or support resource you can contact today and keep that connection within reach.

entries.title: Make Room for Peace — Romans 15:13
entries.excerpt: A slower breath can interrupt urgency and reopen the space where wise choices live.
entries.body: Romans 15:13 says, “Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope in the power of the Holy Spirit.” Peace does not require pretending that the craving or pressure is small. It lets you pause long enough to remember that the feeling is temporary and that you are not facing it alone. Let this verse shape the next decision rather than asking it to fix the entire journey at once.
entries.prayer: God of peace, quiet the urgency in me and guard my thoughts while I wait for this moment to pass.
entries.practice: Take five slow breaths, then delay any impulsive choice for ten minutes.
